title: [design] export-qasm reference lowering is ~1000x too large for compiled oracles; needs an engineered exporter with the current lowering kept as oracle
description:
Maintainer verdict 2026-11-09 ~16:5xZ (via advisor): the exporter is 'not fit for purpose'. This is a DESIGN bead, not a performance fix.

Back-of-envelope on the Collatz oracle (54-line lproc, 64-bit registers): the current construction emits ~10^6 gate nodes per budget step (measured ~110 MB IR/step), i.e. ~2e9 gates at B=2048. Dominated by (a) full call/return stack machinery emitted every step for a depth-1 call (~1.5e5 Toffolis/step); (b) a generic 64x64 multiplier for 'mul' by constant 3 and a 64-stage barrel shifter for 'lshr' by constant 1; (c) every row re-emitted every step because possible_successors("ret") returns all rows.
A sensible step-unrolled exporter (inline single calls, fold constant operands, emit only reachable rows per step, stream output, explicit garbage/uncompute strategy) is ~2e3 gates/step, ~4e6 gates at B=2048; a loop-level circuit would be ~4e5.

Required deliverable: a design doc in bennett-circuits/docs/design/ plus a council (oracle/contract class, COMMON rule 7: it changes what 'the circuit for an oracle' is, while the ISA semantics must stay identical) BEFORE any implementation child. The existing lowering stays as the differential oracle for small budgets. Rule 9: sizes and acceptance in work units (gates, nodes), never seconds. Queue: behind the Grover items. Measured hotspots of the current lowering: bennett-circuits-55q (still true, not the fix).

Evidence (advisor, measured 2026-11-09 16:1x-16:4xZ on Spiral, circuits main 7b7f99f built in a scratchpad): object = 54-line Collatz lproc oracle (toy2/plg/out/ref.bennett from the pitch explainer; copy /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-bennett-workspace/27562397-a9c0-4989-b62b-243d71b11e66/scratchpad/toy2/plg/out/ref.bennett; evidence dir /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-bennett-workspace/58185567-d6f9-491c-bb78-59182f3686b7/scratchpad/circ: b*.err, bt.err, perf2.data, syms.txt; scratchpad paths are ephemeral, copy before relying on them). check and hash on the object: 0.00 s. export-qasm --budget 32,0,32,32: 3.5 GB RSS in 21 s, then alloc failure under a 4 GB cap (backtrace Build::flip <- copy <- exchange <- Machine::array_exchange <- row <- forward). Budgets 1, 2, 4: 437 MB flat, no output after 120 s; budget 1 still no output after 10 min. Budget 8: 931 MB at 120 s. So ~110 MB of IR per budget step plus a super-linear time cost independent of budget. Structural cause of the memory: possible_successors("ret") returns every row, so after the first return every step re-emits all ~35 rows incl. the 64-bit mul (64 adders): ~1M gates/step; 4096 steps ~ 450 GB. Red-first: this object at budget 1. Rule 9: any fix and its regression are stated in work units (gates, nodes emitted per step), never seconds.
